title: Finite scalar comparison preserves derived reduction adjuncts
statement:
Let $\mathcal C$ be a small site and let $R\xrightarrow{\varphi}B\xrightarrow{\psi}S$ be morphisms of sheaves of commutative rings. Use module sheaves and their unbounded derived categories [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category, def-weil-abstract-derived-category], exact restriction of scalars $\operatorname{Res}_{B/R}$ [def-pc-sheaf-restrict-scalars], and K-flat derived scalar extension [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings]. Assume $B$ is flat over $R$, meaning that $B\otimes_R-$ is exact, and that the multiplication map $B\otimes_R S\to S$, $b\otimes s\mapsto\psi(b)s$, is an isomorphism of sheaves.

For every $M\in D(B)$ the canonical balanced comparison is a natural isomorphism in $D(S)$,
$$\kappa_{M,S}:(\operatorname{Res}_{B/R}M)\otimes_R^L S\xrightarrow{\sim}M\otimes_B^L S.$$
It is represented on a K-flat $B$-complex with flat terms by $x\otimes s\mapsto x\otimes s$. Give all scalar extensions their canonical derived extension--restriction adjunctions [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-module-adjunction, lem-pc-derived-adjoint-functors]. For every $Q\in D(S)$ and $p:M\to\operatorname{Res}_{S/B}Q$, let $p_B^\sharp:M\otimes_B^L S\to Q$ be its adjunct and let $p_R^\sharp:(\operatorname{Res}_{B/R}M)\otimes_R^L S\to Q$ be the adjunct of $\operatorname{Res}_{B/R}(p)$. Then
$$p_R^\sharp=p_B^\sharp\circ\kappa_{M,S}.$$
The comparisons commute with a morphism $S\to S'$ of $B$-algebras whenever the same multiplication-isomorphism hypothesis holds for $S'$. They also commute with successive derived scalar extensions from $S$ to $S'$ under the canonical scalar-extension associativity isomorphisms; equal-index comparison uses the canonical scalar-extension unit identification.

proof.text: Construct the ordinary balanced comparison using [lem-pbc-ordinary-flat-coefficient-comparison]. Its inverse after restriction is tensor cancellation followed by tensoring the assumed multiplication isomorphism. The comparison sends each scalar-first pure tensor s tensor x to s tensor x, without using flatness.

Restriction is exact by [lem-pur-sheaf-ring-derived-coefficient-adjunction]. If P is K-flat over B and has flat terms, [lem-pur-change-of-rings-tensor-cancellation-independent] identifies A tensor_R Res(P) with Res((B tensor_R A) tensor_B P), degreewise and after totalization. Flatness makes B tensor_R A acyclic and K-flatness of P makes the latter tensor acyclic; exact restriction preserves acyclicity. Restriction preserves the total sums because its underlying abelian-sheaf functor preserves colimits [lem-weil-pbc-module-sheaves-colimits-forgetful]. The same cancellation exhibits tensoring with Res(P^i) as a composite of three exact functors. The tensor-functor identification [lem-weil-pbc-independent-sheaf-tensor-colimits] translates this to IsFlatOnSite. This proves both restricted K-flatness and restricted flat terms.

Using the adjunctions and composition isomorphisms supplied as Normalization data [def-pbc-successive-derived-scalar-normalization-data], define kappa_M as delta(phi,psi)^{-1} at Res(M), followed by extension of the adjunction counit for phi. Naturality is the naturality of delta and of the counit. The normalized composition unit and the adjunction triangle identity show that the R-adjunct of kappa_M followed by the B-adjunct of f is Res(f) followed by composite restriction. Injectivity of the R-adjunction gives the required adjunct identity for every derived morphism.

For a flat-term K-flat P, normalize the derived hom bijections using Normalization.adjunction_normalization and both localization counits. The ordinary pure formula identifies the ordinary unit composites, degreewise and on the homotopy quotient. Normalization.rightComp_normalization identifies the restriction factors. Applying the R-adjunction bijection to both sides proves the required universal-counit representative formula. The two computation counits are invertible by step 2 and Normalization.computed; all the other representative factors are isomorphisms, so kappa is invertible at the localization of P.

Resolve any homotopy object by a flat-term K-flat complex [lem-pc-kflat-resolution]. Localization inverts the resulting quasi-isomorphism, and naturality transports invertibility of kappa to that object. Essential surjectivity of the homotopy localization then transports it to every derived object [lem-weil-pbc-localization-universal-property]. Assemble the pointwise invertible natural transformation into a natural isomorphism.

Expand the counit-defined kappa. Naturality of delta and the associative normalization [def-pbc-successive-derived-scalar-normalization-data] prove the successive compatibility. Apply naturality of the next adjunction unit to obtain coefficient naturality with exactly the specified coefficient-change arrows. Specialize successive compatibility to the identity ring map and use eqToHom naturality along the right-unit equality to obtain the equal-index identity. Assemble these identities, the ordinary isomorphism, and the computation result into the unchanged FlatCoefficientReductionComparison.

split_report.summary: Flat restriction preserves the chosen K-flat model by the cancellation identity and exactness. Multiplication B tensor_R S = S gives the explicit balanced chain comparison. All ingredients already have DAG nodes; no new node and no statement change.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-NK-ef5dad566 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read all 8 steps and the 12 cited statements in full. The delivery has no new nodes, and the item's statement and stmt_deps are byte-equal to live. The item is unsplit on live and side-live, nothing it touches is in the dropped lists, and there is no SGA source. The statement holds: (Res M)⊗^L_R S ≅ M⊗^L_B (B⊗_R S) ≅ M⊗^L_B S. Small cases checked: R=B gives κ=id; Z→Z[1/2]→F_3 gives the obvious identification; Z→F_p (B not flat) and k→k[t]→k (μ not an isomorphism) both give an extra Tor_1, so each hypothesis is needed. The S′ hypothesis is in fact automatic, since B⊗_R S′ ≅ (B⊗_R S)⊗_S S′ ≅ S′. Step 2 uses the cancellation with M=P^i over B and N=A^j over R, the colimit/forget node for sums and acyclicity, and the exact-functor node for acyclicity of B⊗A; this gives K-flatness and flat terms. Step 3 writes balanced inverse formulas whose S-linearity can be checked directly. Step 4 uses derived change of rings (1),(2) on UP and P, plus descent through W^{-1}P_B≃D(B) and the localization universal property. Steps 5-6 use the unit normalization (1) for ψ and ψφ, then Hom-equivalence injectivity; this proves the adjunct equation for arbitrary derived p. Step 7 is the sectionwise square x⊗τ(s). Step 8 uses kflat-change-of-rings and the stated associator formula of lem-sfb-successive-derived-quotient-normalization, which holds for arbitrary ring maps; the iterated case and the unit were checked. Sources checked: Stacks 06YS, 0G7E (l.3508), 05V4 (l.4610) and the other tags, plus the main-20261015 proof of the parent, whose steps use exactly the three clauses. No duplicate found among roughly 10 candidate scalar-comparison nodes. The tool uses are generic K-flat, tensor and adjunction lemmas and are accepted. Advisories, not faults: (1) the item's 'canonical' adjunctions are read as the normalized lem-pur-sheaf-ring-derived-coefficient-adjunction; the two agree because both units are x↦x⊗1 on K-flat models. (2) def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules is not cited in step 2, but the step writes out what flat means.
